question: Should OpenClaw core own this opt-in model-elected continuation system, including trusted cross-session delegate returns behind crossSessionTargeting, once conflicts and the status-row defect are fixed?
rationale: The implementation is broad, persisted, config-visible, and touches session/security boundaries; code review can verify mechanics but cannot decide whether this belongs in core now versus a narrower or experimental surface.

options.title: Approve guarded core ownership
options.body: Land the feature after conflict resolution, the status-row fix, and current-head proof for any behavior-affecting conflict changes, keeping continuation disabled and cross-session targeting default-deny.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require a smaller first merge that excludes cross-session targeting or selected continuation modes until those policy boundaries are separately reviewed.

options.title: Pause or close as too broad
options.body: Defer the PR if maintainers do not want this much scheduler/session/state policy in core at this time.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core ownership
recommendation.body: Land the feature after conflict resolution, the status-row fix, and current-head proof for any behavior-affecting conflict changes, keeping continuation disabled and cross-session targeting default-deny.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the continuation shape and explicitly called out crossSessionTargeting default-deny as a maintainer-deferred decision.
